html:
Swahili, or Kiswahili, is a Bantu language that grew on the East African coast from around the 8th to 10th centuries and is now spoken by tens of millions of people across East and Central Africa.

It developed in the trading towns of the Swahili coast, borrowing many words from Arabic, and later from Persian, Portuguese and English. It was written in Arabic script for centuries, as in the poetry of the Utendi wa Tambuka, and in Latin letters from the 19th century.

Caravans carried it inland, and German and British rulers used it in government. After independence Nyerere made it the national language of Tanzania, and it became a link language in Kenya, Uganda and Congo. It is an official language of the African Union.
sum: Swahili, or Kiswahili, is a Bantu language that grew on the East African coast from around the 8th to 10th centuries and is now spoken by tens of millions of people across East and Central Africa.
